Republican [[John G. Rowland]] won the open seat following the retirement of [[A Connecticut Party]] Governor [[Lowell Weicker]]. The election was a four-way race between A Connecticut Party Lieutenant Governor [[Eunice Groark]], Republican U.S. Congressman John G. Rowland, Democratic state comptroller [[Bill Curry (politician)|Bill Curry]], and independent conservative talk show host [[Tom Scott (Connecticut politician)|Tom Scott]]. Rowland won the election with just 36% of the vote.{{cite web |url=http://www.ct.gov/sots/lib/sots/electionservices/statementofvote_pdfs/1994_sov.pdf |title=Summary of Vote for Governor and Lieutenant Governor |publisher=Office of the Connecticut Secretary of the State |format=PDF |date=November 13, 1994 |access-date=October 13, 2010 |archive-date=October 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015212235/http://www.ct.gov/sots/lib/sots/electionservices/statementofvote_pdfs/1994_sov.pdf |url-status=dead }} As a result of Public Act 93-342, which was passed by the [[Connecticut General Assembly|General Assembly]] in 1993, the threshold of delegate support a candidate required at a nominating convention in order to force a primary was reduced from 20% to 15%, making this the first election held under these new laws.{{cite web |url=https://www.cga.ct.gov/2001/rpt/2001-R-0953.htm |title=Legislative History of Challenge Primary Law |publisher=Connecticut General Assembly |date=December 18, 2001 |author=Mary M.
